# relizy

> relizy 2.0.1-beta.0 is installed: these rules and the docs in `node_modules/relizy/agent-docs` match this version.

This project releases with **relizy**: versions, changelogs, git tags, npm publishing and GitHub/GitLab releases, computed from the commits and configured in `relizy.config.ts`.

### Look it up before you guess

- **MCP server `relizy`** (when available): `preview_release` (what the next release bumps and why), `preview_changelog`, `lint_commit`, `get_project` (resolved config, version mode, groups, packages), `get_config_option`, `search_docs`, `get_doc`, `check_migration` (what to change to upgrade from relizy 1).
- **Version-matched docs** in `node_modules/relizy/agent-docs/` (start with `README.md`).

Never invent a config option nor a CLI flag: check it with `get_config_option` or the docs.

### Commits drive the releases

- Write [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org): `type(scope): subject`. The type decides the bump and the changelog section: `feat` is a minor, `fix` and `perf` a patch, `!` after the type or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer a major (the `types` of the config can change this).
- Lint the message before committing: `lint_commit` or `relizy commitlint --message "<message>"`. It also shows the changelog entry the commit produces.
- In a monorepo, a commit belongs to the packages whose files it changes: one package (or one concern) per commit gives precise bumps and changelogs.
- The body of a commit can end up in the changelog: write it for the users of the package.

### Releasing

- Preview, never guess: `preview_release` and `preview_changelog`, or `relizy release --dry-run`.
- Never run `relizy release`, `bump`, `publish`, `changelog`, `provider-release`, `social` or `pr-comment` without the explicit approval of the user: they write versions and changelogs, commit, tag, push and publish. Most projects release from their CI.
- Never edit the versions of the `package.json` files, the `CHANGELOG.md` files nor the release tags by hand: relizy computes them from the commits and the tags.

### Configuration

- `defineConfig` from `relizy` types `relizy.config.ts`. Several configs can coexist (`relizy.<name>.config.ts`, selected with `--config <name>`).
- Monorepos: `monorepo.versionMode` is `unified`, `selective` (one version, only the changed packages) or `independent`; `monorepo.groups` releases several sets of packages, each with its own mode.
- Set up a new project with `relizy init` (`--yes` without questions), and the AI agents with `relizy mcp init`.
